title: Foundry CMOS platform for multimodal quantum materials characterization
authors: Sharad Kumar Yadav, Luca Nessi, Ondrej Dyck, Jinchen Wang, Bogdan Dryzhakov, Alex Melendez, Huan Zhao, Qian Song, Doha Amer, Cole Brabec, Saleh Alqazlan, Ruonan Han, Riccardo Comin, Stephen Jesse, Dirk Englund, Jawaher Almutlaq
abstract: Quantum materials experiments increasingly rely on microwave, electrical, thermal, optical, and structural probes, but these capabilities are typically assembled from custom hardware that limits reproducibility and scalability. Here we show that a commercial 65-nm CMOS process can be repurposed as a passive, foundry-manufacturable characterization platform by functionally partitioning its metal stack into microwave, thermal, and electrical subsystems within a 1 mm2 footprint. The integrated RF architecture enables cryogenic magnetic susceptibility measurements of Fe3GeTe2 heterostructures at 1.75 K without sample-specific fabrication. We further demonstrate NV-center optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) with >20% contrast at 4-9 dBm microwave power, reducing power requirements by 20-25 dB relative to conventional antenna-based approaches while maintaining sensitivities of 2-3 uT/sqrt(Hz). We additionally confirm compatibility with in-situ electron-beam imaging, showing no measurable degradation in image quality upon device operation. These results establish a scalable, foundry-manufacturable platform for multimodal quantum sensing and materials characterization.
summary: This work introduces a novel, scalable characterization platform built using standard 65-nm CMOS technology to measure multiple physical properties (microwave, thermal, electrical) simultaneously. By integrating these functions onto a single chip, the authors overcome limitations in reproducibility and scalability inherent in current bespoke experimental setups. This breakthrough enables more accessible and standardized quantum materials research.
main_problem: Current quantum materials characterization methods are limited by custom, non-scalable hardware setups that cannot easily integrate multiple measurement modalities.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a scalable, foundry-manufacturable CMOS platform capable of integrating microwave, thermal, and electrical probes for multimodal quantum sensing.
method: They repurposed a commercial 65-nm CMOS process to functionally partition the metal stack into distinct subsystems within a small footprint.
model_or_system: The physical system is an integrated chip built on a standard CMOS foundry platform, featuring interdigitated electrodes (IDEs) for electrical sensing and patterned inductors for microwave excitation. This allows for heterogeneous integration of various quantum measurements.
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), ODMR contrast ($>20\%$), $	ext{S}$-parameters, capacitance-voltage ($	ext{C–V}$) response, and SEM image sharpness metrics.
important_parameters: Operating temperatures down to $1.75 	ext{ K}$, microwave power levels of $4–9 	ext{ dBm}$, and a platform size limited to $1 	ext{ mm}^2$.
main_assumptions: The approach relies on repurposing existing commercial CMOS back-end-of-line capabilities, and magnetic measurements involve transferring samples onto the chip.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic architecture partitioning (Fig 1), detailed measurement results including $	ext{S}$-parameters, $	ext{C–V}$ curves, and temperature dependence of susceptibility (Fig 2); ODMR benchmarking compares CMOS vs. antenna setups (Fig 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for scalable multimodal characterization to presenting measurements across multiple domains: RF/Microwave ($	ext{S}$-params, ODMR), Electrical ($	ext{C–V}$ on IDEs), and Thermal (resistance vs. T), culminating in a demonstration of integrated functionality.
why_interesting: The development of standardized, foundry-compatible hardware platforms is crucial for advancing quantum science by removing significant engineering bottlenecks associated with custom cryogenic setups.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
